svg.title: Strictly henselian local rings and a nonzero global class
svg.desc: X is the connected spectrum of the algebraic integers. Its local rings are all strictly henselian. The closed subset V(6) partitions into the nonempty pieces V(2) and V(3). A constant global value restricts to equal values on those pieces. The section one on V(2) and zero on V(3) has a nonzero boundary in first cohomology of the constant group of order two extended by zero from D(6). Constant finite cohomology on X vanishes, but this other torsion sheaf is not acyclic.
svg.metadata: Creator: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI). CC0. Proof: Theorem J.1.5.1 and Exercise J.1.9. The two-part constants are a subgroup of all sections on V(6); no equality with that entire group is asserted.
svg.text: Strict local rings and a nonzero global class
R is the integral closure of ℤ in ℚ̄; X = Spec R is connected.
Every local ring of X is strictly henselian.
The closed partition and its unequal section
Z = V(6) = V(2) ⊔ V(3); both pieces are nonempty.
These are whole closed pieces, not individual points.
A constant c on connected X restricts to (c, c), never (1, 0).
The boundary is the actual nonzero class
j: D(6) → X; i: Z → X; coefficients are F₂.
Hq(X, F2) = 0 for q > 0; the extended sheaf has nonzero H1.
Étale–Zariski comparison does not imply global acyclicity.
Proof: Theorem J.1.5.1 and the complete solution of Exercise J.1.9.
